item.title: In the same breath 同时；话又说回来
item.description:
节目简介

英语表达 “in the same breath” 的字面意思是 “在同一次呼吸之中”，实际用来表示 “紧接着又说起另一件截然不同，甚至相反的事情”。它可以用来指出前后两种说法之间存在反差，有点类似中文里的 “不过话又说回来”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 学习这个地道表达的含义和用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Becca
And I'm Becca.

Feifei
Becca, last time we caught up, we were talking about your plans for the end of the month. Something about a hike?

Becca
Ah, I remember that conversation. I'm thinking about going away soon, and I was considering a hiking holiday because I haven't done that before, but in the same breath, I feel like I need to just relax.

Feifei
That I understand. You just used 'in the same breath'. What does it mean?

Becca
Well, 'in the same breath' is used to compare different ideas. It introduces a contradiction. Though different, both ideas could be true, but the latter idea, which comes after 'in the same breath', usually carries more weight.

Feifei
I see. So, as much as you'd like to try something new and go on a hiking holiday, you mostly just want to relax. And you used the coordinating conjunction 'but' before the expression.

Becca
Yes. Conjunctions that show contrast, such as 'but', 'however' and 'though', can be used before 'in the same breath' to introduce the differences between the ideas.

Feifei
Right. Let's hear some more examples.

Examples
My friend says she hates her job, but then in the same breath, she's just volunteered for more overtime.

You said you wanted to help me, but then in the same breath, you say you've got no time, you can't do it. I mean, which is it?

My friend says she's run out of money, but in the same breath, she just told me that she's booked a really expensive holiday. What's going on?

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “in the same breath” 的用法。“In the same breath” 的字面意思是 “在同一次呼吸之中”，而它实际上的作用则是引出与前文形成对比甚至略显矛盾的另一种看法或观点，意思相当于 “话又说回来”。所以，在使用这个表达的时候，我们常会搭配 “but”、“however”、“though” 等表示转折的连词，以突出两种想法之间的对比。比如，我们可能会说 “though in the same breath” 或者 “but in the same breath”。

Becca, are there any other phrases or expressions that mean the same thing or could be used like 'in the same breath'?

Becca
Well, you might have heard of 'on the other hand', 'at the same time' or 'in the same instance'. These phrases are fairly common and express a difference.

Feifei
和 “in the same breath” 类似的表达还有 “on the other hand”、“at the same time” 和 “in the same instance”。这些表达都比较常见，可以用来引出与前文不同或形成对比的观点。

Becca
That's it for this programme, but join us next time to learn more English phrases and expressions. Bye for now!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: Leave to one's own devices 让某人自行决定，不加干预
item.description:
节目简介

你会选择放手让别人自己解决问题吗？有时，这是出于信任和鼓励；有时，却可能显得缺乏责任感。英语表达 “leave someone to their own devices” 就可以用来形容 “让某人依靠自己的能力独自应对或处理问题”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 一起学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
Your lunch looks interesting today.

Phil
Yeah, my kids made it for me. It's leftovers from yesterday's dinner.

Feifei
They cooked it on their own?

Phil
Yes, they really wanted to make something. We just left them to their own devices, and they looked up a recipe, bought the ingredients and made it – all on their own.

Feifei
You used the expression 'leave to their own devices'. I think we should have a look at that. It's a really interesting one. But it's got nothing to do with devices, has it?

Phil
Well, certainly not in the way that we use that word today. If you are left to your own devices, it means that you're left on your own. Sometimes, we use it to say that we trust people enough to do things on their own. We also sometimes use it to talk about being left without any help.

Feifei
So, you were able to leave your kids to their own devices because you trusted them. Another example is, if your boss gives you a massive piece of work and doesn't explain anything about it, you might be unhappy that you've been left to your own devices.

Phil
Let's hear some more people using the expression 'leave to one's own devices'.

Examples
The flight from Seoul was delayed for about two hours. We didn't have any information. They just left us to our own devices.

I've got a few things to do before everyone else arrives. So can I just leave you to your own devices for a bit?

Oh, I really love being left to my own devices, which is why I enjoy working from home so much.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “leave to one's own devices” 的用法。“Leave to one's own devices” 的意思是 “让某人依靠自己的能力和资源独立处理问题或面对挑战”。

要注意的是，“leave to one's own devices” 本身是一个中性表达。它既可以表示 “出于信任而让某人自主发挥”，也可以表示 “没有给予应有的帮助或指导，让某人不得不独自应对困难处境”。

Phil
We said that one meaning was 'to be left on your own without any help', and another expression that has meaning is 'to be left to fend for oneself'.

Feifei
我们还可以用 “to be left to fend for oneself” 来表达和 “leave to one's own devices” 类似的负面含义，意思是 “被迫独自照顾自己、解决问题，没有人提供帮助”。

Phil
Well, this is the end of the programme, but we're not just going to leave you to your own devices. We'll back next time to help you learn more English phrases and expressions.

Feifei
See you then.

Phil
Bye!

item.title: Try one's patience 考验某人的耐心
item.description:
节目简介

如果有一件事特别烦人，让你不得不努力克制情绪、保持耐心，那么它就在 “trying your patience”。英语表达 “try one's patience” 非常实用，其中 “try” 的意思不是 “尝试”，而是 “test（考验，检验）”。所以，“try one's patience” 的意思就是 “考验某人的耐心”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 一起学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
I saw you struggling with the printer earlier, are you OK?

Phil
I hate those machines!

Feifei
You seemed quite annoyed.

Phil
I can't stand it – paper jammed, open this bit, close this bit, put something in here, take something out of here. No ink. They really try my patience.

Feifei
I mean you should try patience. You need to calm down a bit.

Phil
Oh, no, I said "try my patience". In this expression, 'try' has a similar meaning to 'test'. If something tries your patience, it means you get to see how patient, or impatient, you really are.

Feifei
Don't worry, I was just joking with you. Yes, 'try one's patience' is a great expression to talk about things that annoy you. If something tries your patience, then it's something annoying. You get to see how much you can tolerate before you lose your patience – which didn't seem to be very long when you were using that printer.

Phil
Yes, you might be right there. It's an expression that can be used about anything that makes you annoyed, whether that's bad traffic, annoying colleagues or terrible customer service. All of these things can try your patience.

Feifei
Let's hear some more people using the expression 'try one's patience'.

Examples
Excuse me, can you sit down? Sit down! You're really trying my patience.

My computer just keeps crashing. It's really trying my patience now.

"Unknown item in bagging area." Aargh, these self-checkouts really try my patience.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “try one's patience” 的用法。动词 “try” 在这个表达中的意思是 “test”，也就是 “考验，检验”，所以 “try one's patience” 指的就是 “考验、挑战某人的耐心”。

比如，当一件事情给我带来不便、困扰，甚至痛苦，需要我拿出十足的耐心和冷静来应对，甚至让我快要失去耐心、大发脾气的时候，我就可以说： “It's trying my patience.”。

Phil
This expression often gets used in the negative, almost as a warning. 'Don't try my patience – you are going to need my help'. We can also use 'Don't try your luck' or 'Don't push your luck' in a similar way.

Feifei
是的。我们还可以用 “don't try my patience” 来警告别人 “别考验我的耐心，别故意惹我”。和这个用法类似的表达还有 “don't try your luck” 和 “don't push your luck”。

Phil
We're at the end of programme but do come back next time. We can help you improve your English without trying your patience.

Feifei
See you next time!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: Sack something off 放弃计划，临时取消安排
item.description:
节目简介

单词 “sack” 作动词时有 “解雇，开除” 的含义。那么，“sack something off” 的意思难道是 “把某物开除”？其实不然！英式俚语 “sack something off” 的意思是 “因为没时间、犯懒或有了其它安排而临时取消原定计划”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
Feifei, I am exhausted, and sadly I've got plans every night this week. Big error!

Feifei
Oh no! What are you going to do?

Georgie
Well, I think I'm going to sack off some of the bigger plans and just hope that my friends don't mind too much.

Feifei
That sounds like a sensible idea. You need to rest! Now, that's a good phrasal verb to learn – sack something off. What does it mean?

Georgie
Well, in this case, sack off plans means cancel plans. More broadly, it can mean to stop or avoid doing something because you feel too lazy or you'd rather be doing something else.

Feifei
Right. I'm supposed to be going to the gym later, but I'd rather sack that off and watch TV.

Georgie
Great example! Let's hear more from our BBC Learning English colleagues.

Examples
The work training is optional and it's so boring, so I decided to sack it off and get some coffee instead.

We booked a walking tour in Paris, but we were so tired after our flight that we decided to sack it off.

I needed to get some ingredients in for dinner, but I was kind of feeling lazy, so I decided to sack it off and get a takeaway instead.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习短语动词 “sack off” 的用法。“Sack off” 是一个英式俚语表达。其中，单词 “sack” 本身有 “解雇；抛弃” 的含义。在英式英语中，人们会用 “sack off” 来表示 “放弃原本打算完成的事情”或者“取消事先安排好的计划”。

使用这个短语动词的时候，说话人往往是在暗示 “自己因为想偷懒、没时间或者有其它安排而不想继续执行原定计划”。所以，这个表达通常带有一点随意、懒散，甚至不太积极的意味。

Georgie, how can we use 'sack off'?

Georgie
Well, 'sack off' is a separable phrasal verb, which means that you can put an object at the end of the verb or in the middle. So, you can say 'sack off a plan' or 'sack a plan off'.

Feifei
“Sack off” 是一个可以被分隔的短语动词。比如，在表示 “取消一项计划” 的时候，我们既可以说 “sack off a plan”，也可以说 “sack a plan off”。

Georgie
Feifei, shall we sack off the rest of this programme?!

Feifei
No, Georgie! We just have to do the recap and then we're done. Don't be lazy.

Georgie
You're right, you're right. OK. We learnt 'sack something off' which means to cancel something, avoid or stop doing something. See you again next time!

Feifei
Thanks for joining us. Bye-bye!

Georgie
Bye!

item.title: In a tizzy 慌里慌张，大惊小怪
item.description:
节目简介

当他人因为一些其实没什么大不了的事情而变得惊慌失措、手忙脚乱，仿佛和平时判若两人时，英国人常会开玩笑地说：“Don't get yourself in a tizzy!”。表达 “in a tizzy” 或 “in a tizz” 形容的就是一个人因小事而过度慌乱、紧张、震惊或兴奋的状态，相当于中文里的 “慌了神” 或 “乱了阵脚”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
I'm very well, thank you Feifei. How are you?

Feifei
I'm well, thank you Georgie. So, the expression we're learning in this programme is 'in a tizzy'. What does it mean to be in a tizzy?

Georgie
Well, I actually used this the other day. My sister was getting stressed because she lost her house keys. I said to her, 'Don't get yourself in a tizzy. I saw you with them yesterday. They'll be in the house'. In the UK, it's also common to say, 'in a tizz'.

Feifei
Right, so if you're in a tizzy, it means you're in a state of panic or confusion. So, when you said to your sister, 'Don't get yourself in a tizzy', it's like saying 'don't worry'.

Georgie
Yes exactly, but when you're in a tizzy, it's usually over something minor, and the reaction is often bigger than the problem requires. I'm quite a calm person, so I don't often get myself in a tizzy. What gets you in a tizz, Feifei?

Feifei
Well, in the morning, if I miss my train and then I'm late for work, that gets me in a tizz. OK, Georgie, time for some more examples.

Examples
I got myself in a right tizzy yesterday when my crush didn't respond to my text. Turns out, they were just busy with work.

I lost my friends at a concert. I was in a right tizzy, but then I saw them dancing at the edge of the crowd.

I got myself in a tizzy when I thought I would fail the driving test, but when we got out of the car, the examiner told me that I'd passed!

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “in a tizzy” 的用法。“In a tizzy”，或者英国人更常说的 “in a tizz”，通常用来形容一个人 “有些慌乱、紧张、震惊或兴奋，以至于失去了平日的冷静”，而造成这种反应的原因往往并不是什么大不了的事。

这个表达的语气十分幽默，因此人们用它来调侃别人 “反应过度，有些大惊小怪”，或者提醒对方 “Don't get yourself in a tizzy（别瞎着急，冷静点）”。

Georgie, what else do we need to know about 'in a tizzy'?

Georgie
Well, there are some other useful, similar expressions. 'I'm in a tizz' can mean the same as 'I'm flustered' or 'I'm worked up'.

Feifei
除了用来形容别人，我们也可以用 “I'm in a tizz” 或者 “I'm in a tizzy” 来表示 “我有点慌乱” 或 “我有点晕头转向、不知所措”。

Georgie
OK, let's recap. 'In a tizzy' or 'in a tizz' means in a state of worry over something minor. Join us again next time for another useful expression.

Feifei
See you then. Goodbye!

Georgie
Bye-bye!

item.title: Same person, different font 仿佛一个模子里刻出来的人
item.description:
节目简介

世界之大，我们可能会遇到两个性格、行为方式，甚至气质都极其相似的人。在英语中，人们会用表达 “same person, different font” 来形容这种相似感，意思是 “两个人仿佛是一个模子里刻出来的，就像同一段文字只是换了不同字体一样”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 学习这个表达的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Becca
And I'm Becca.

Feifei
Becca, I met our new colleague today. She reminds me of you!

Becca
Really? That's interesting. We have quite different personalities and upbringings.

Feifei
Well, you both have curly hair, dress in soft colours and talk incredibly fast.

Becca
OK. Maybe we're the same person, different font!

Feifei
'Same person, different font'? That's a strange expression.

Becca
It is! It's a humorous way of saying that two people are very similar in some ways, but are still clearly different people.

Feifei
So, it's like they have the same style or appearance, but there are differences in the details?

Becca
Exactly. Think about two versions of the same piece of writing in different fonts. The words are the same, but they look different. When we describe people as 'the same person, different font', or 'the same person in a different font', we're joking that they have a very similar vibe.

Feifei
I see. Let's hear some more examples.

Examples
When my brother calls me on the phone, he sounds exactly like my dad. They're really the same person, just different font.

You remind me so much of someone I went to school with. It's like you're the same person, different font.

My friend and I are really similar. It's like we are the same person, just a different font.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “same person, different font” 的用法。“Same person, different font” 的字面意思是 “同一个人，不同的字体”。可是，人又不是文字，怎么会有不同的 “font（字体）” 呢？所以，这个表达其实是在用这种方式来比喻 “两个人的本质、性格或行为方式极其相似，散发出来的气场一模一样，就好像是同一段文字，换了两种不同的字体呈现出来一样”。

So, it doesn't always mean that the people look alike.

Becca
Correct. They might look completely different – in that case, it's more about their personality, behaviour, interests or general style.

Feifei
Becca, is this a very common expression?

Becca
It's fairly common in spoken English, and you might see it online or on social media. It's informal. I could say, if I ever met someone who is very organised, stylish and has a bob haircut…

Feifei
Oh, you might have found me in a different font! That's it for this programme, but join us next time to learn more English phrases and expressions. Goodbye!

Becca
Bye!

item.title: A hot take 大胆且容易引发争议的观点
item.description:
节目简介

单词 “take” 作名词时，可以表示 “看法、观点”。表达 “a hot take” 指的是 “一个颇为大胆，非主流、可能引发争议的观点”。不过，“a hot take” 也不一定真的是一个语出惊人的独到见解，因为不少人会用它来提出一个其实十分普通甚至有些无聊的观点，以达到幽默调侃的效果。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Becca 学习如何使用这个表达。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Becca
And I'm Becca.

Feifei
Becca, I can't help but notice that you're wearing flip-flops with socks?

Becca
Well, my work shoes got so wet in the rain yesterday, and I didn't want to show my toes at work!

Feifei
Oh! Socks with flip-flops could be considered uncommon here in the UK, you know. It could be common in some places, but I know some people here find it really odd.

Becca
Well, I've got a hot take – socks and flip-flops are comfy, and everyone should wear something like this inside.

Feifei
'A hot take'? That sounds quite dramatic!

Becca
It does, doesn't it? 'A hot take' is simply a controversial or surprising opinion. It's something you say when you think other people might disagree with you.

Feifei
So, I could say, 'I don't know if this is a hot take, but I think pineapple belongs on pizza'?

Becca
You could definitely say that! Especially if you're talking to someone who is passionate about cooking authentic cuisine. They could be pretty mad at you for saying that!

Feifei
Let's hear some more examples.

Examples
I don't know if this is a hot take, but I don't like going on holiday in the summer. I prefer to go in the winter months when it's cooler.

My hot take is that chocolate is overrated – you think you like it, but you don't really.

I always prefer the film adaptations to the books. Anyway, that's just my hot take.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习流行表达 “a hot take” 的用法。这个表达中的 “take” 是名词，意思是 “看法，态度”，而形容词 “hot” 在这里则表示 “容易引发讨论或争议的”。因此，表达 “a hot take” 指的就是 “一个颇为大胆、非主流、可能引发争议的观点”。

Becca, it seems 'a hot take' is an informal expression?

Becca
Yep! You might hear it online, on social media, in podcasts or in conversations with friends. It's often used to introduce an opinion that's likely to cause a negative reaction.

Feifei
So, you can say 'hot take' or 'I've got a hot take' before giving your opinion, almost like a warning.

Becca
Exactly. And here's an interesting thing about 'a hot take'. 'A hot take' doesn't necessarily have to be completely outrageous. Sometimes people jokingly call an ordinary opinion 'a hot take' because they know it might start a debate.

Feifei
我们需要注意的是，使用 “a hot take” 这个表达并不意味着这个观点就一定是错误的。它更多指的是一种 “相对少见、略显大胆或容易引发大家讨论和争议的看法”。

除此之外，人们有时候也会带着幽默或调侃的语气来使用 “a hot take”，故意把一个再普通不过、几乎没有争议的观点说成是 “惊人见解”，以达到搞笑的效果。比如：“Hot take – I like milk.（大胆说一句：我喜欢喝牛奶。）” 显然，这个观点大概率不会引发什么争论。正因为它过于平常，所以用 “hot take” 来引出它，反而产生了一种反讽和幽默的效果。

Becca
That's right! Unless you're talking to someone who hates milk or is lactose intolerant.

Feifei
That's true. And, lastly, could I say I have 'a cold take' for opinions that are kind of ordinary and common?

Becca
You could. 'A cold take' is a safe, obvious, or universally agreed-upon opinion that lacks surprise. But I'll say, Feifei, I haven't used the expression 'cold take'.

Feifei
I see. Perhaps it's less common then. 从意思上来说，“a cold take” 可以看作是 “a hot take” 的反义表达，用来形容 “一个非常常见、普遍被接受、几乎不会引发争议的观点”。比如：“Cold take: Exercise is good for your health. （一个毫无争议的观点：锻炼有益健康。）”

不过需要注意的是，“a cold take” 并不是一个特别常用的固定表达。而我们更常用 “a hot take” 来反讽那些其实一点也不 “火爆” 的观点。

Becca
Well, that's it for this programme, but join us next time to learn more English phrases and expressions. But for now, it's goodbye!

Feifei
Goodbye!

item.title: Try it on 耍花招，试探底线
item.description:
节目简介

“Try it on” 的字面意思是 “穿上试试”。在口语中，这个短语不仅可以表示 “试穿” 衣服，还能用来描述 “试图通过耍小聪明、钻空子来达到目的的行为”，甚至还可以表示 “故意提出过分要求，试探他人的底线”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 学习这个短语的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
Are you coming to that meeting later?

Phil
Um, no, I'm leaving early. I'm… erm… going to the airport. I'm going on holiday and I need to get there early.

Feifei
Wait a minute, you're not going on holiday. I don't believe you. You're just trying it on! That important football match is on this afternoon. You just want to go and watch that.

Phil
Maybe… OK, if you promise not to tell anyone else, I'll explain what 'try it on' means here.

Feifei
OK, deal. Everyone knows 'try it on' can be used to talk about clothes. But this is different, isn't it?

Phil
Yes, this is about lying. One meaning of 'try it on' is to try to deceive someone so you don't get in trouble. If someone lies to get out of work early, then they're 'trying it on'.

Feifei
Yes, it's an expression that we often use to challenge someone. This means we often used it in the negative. 'I know you're not going to the airport, don't try it on.'

Phil
Let's hear some more people using 'try it on' in this way.

Examples
My sister said she's got no money and asked to borrow my credit card to buy some food from the shops, but I saw a massive parcel with her name on it. She's just trying it on.

So, the waiter in the restaurant I went to last night didn't bring me back any change after I paid. They said that they'd just forgotten, but I think they were trying it on.

My landlord raised my rent by £100 without telling me. They're definitely trying it on.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习短语 “try it on” 的用法。动词 “try” 的意思是 “尝试”。“Try it on” 原本的含义很简单，指的就是 “在挑选衣服的时候穿上试试”。不过，在口语中，“try it on” 也可以表示某人 “试图通过欺骗、装无辜或耍小聪明来达到目的”。比如，如果你觉得一个人在故意编造借口、夸大事实或试图蒙骗你的时候，你就可以说对方是在 “trying it on”。

Phil
Yes. And it also has another meaning. 'Try it on' can also mean to behave badly to test someone's limits.

Feifei
“Try it on” 不仅可以表示 “试图通过欺骗他人来达到目的”，还可以形容 “故意惹事、无理取闹、挑战规则，借此激怒别人或试探对方的底线”。

Phil, you've got teenage children, haven't you?

Phil
Yes, teenagers are notorious for sometimes trying it on to see what their parents will let them do, like using their phones after we've told them to stop. It means I need to say "Don't try it on! I've told you to put your phone away".

Feifei
OK. That's it for this programme but join us again next time. We really can help you improve your English. We're not just trying it on!

Phil
See you next time!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: Non-starter 注定行不通的计划，无法接受的条件
item.description:
节目简介

常有人说：“Well begun is half done（好的开始是成功的一半）”。而在英语中，如果有一个想法太过离谱，听起来 “注定行不通，甚至不值得一试”，就可以用 “non-starter” 来形容。在谈判中，人们还会用 “non-starter” 指那些 “触碰底线、完全无法接受或没有讨论余地的条件”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Phil 学习复合名词 “non-starter” 的用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain phrases and expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them too. I'm Feifei.

Phil
And I'm Phil.

Feifei
What are you working on there, Phil?

Phil
I've been putting together a business idea: mail-order coffee.

Feifei
What's that?

Phil
Yeah, you could have an app, and then when you fancy a coffee, you press a button, and someone makes you one and sends it to you through the post.

Feifei
Um… I think that's the worst business idea I've ever heard. In fact, I'd say that's a complete non-starter.

Phil
Hm… Maybe you're right. I'll have to think of something else. In the meantime, let's look at that expression 'non-starter'. Can you explain it, Feifei?

Feifei
Yes, we describe something as a non-starter if we think it has absolutely no chance of succeeding. I think a mail-order coffee business is pretty much guaranteed to fail – it's a non-starter.

Phil
It's an expression that we can use to talk about a business idea, but it's also something that can be about any plan, project or initiative. We often use the expression to say that something hasn't been approved.

Feifei
Yes. So, it's also what we use to reject a proposal. For example, 'I've seen your suggestion, but I'm sorry, that's a non-starter'.

Let's listen to some other people using the expression 'non-starter'.

Examples
I've got some friends who live in Scotland. They've invited me up to their house for Christmas, which is great. But they want me to go for a freezing cold swim in the sea on Christmas day, and that is a non-starter.

You want me to leave at 6.30 in the morning for this hike? That's a non-starter.

I pitched an idea at work to make a podcast series about monkeys learning English. My boss said it was a non-starter.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “non-starter” 的用法。“Non-starter” 是一个复合名词，字面意思是 “无法开始的事情”。在实际使用中，它常被用来比喻那些 “一开始就注定难以成功、听起来就没有希望实现的计划、提议或想法”。

除此之外，在谈判和讨价还价的时候，我们也可以用 “non-starter” 来描述 “完全无法接受、连考虑余地都没有的条件或提议”。换句话说，如果某个条件触碰了底线，以至于谈判根本无法继续进行，那么这个条件就是一个 “non-starter”。

Phil
Yes, it might come from horse-racing, where a horse that just stays at the start line and refuses to run is described as a 'non-starter'. Literally, it didn't start the race.

Feifei
OK. That's it for this programme but join us again next time. When it comes to ideas, learning English is definitely not a non-starter, and we have lots of different ways to help you!

Phil
See you next time!

Feifei
Bye-bye!

item.title: No notes 无可挑剔，十分完美
item.description:
节目简介

如果学生在作业或考试中表现不佳，老师通常会留下 “notes（批注，评语）”。而当一个人的表现 “无可挑剔，近乎完美” 时，我们就可以用 “no notes” 来形容。“No notes” 还有哪些地道的用法？听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起学习吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you? Have you had a good week so far?

Georgie
I really have, actually. I went to a concert, it was one of my favourite bands, and the singer was incredible. My sister even put me on her shoulders for my favourite song. I loved it – no notes. How about you?

Feifei
That sounds brilliant, Georgie! I'm having a great week too. The weather's been lovely, I've managed to get all my work done on time, and I've even had time to meet friends after work! No notes.

Georgie
That sounds wonderful, Feifei. I'm so happy for you! Now, let's learn the expression 'no notes'.

Feifei
Yes. Use 'no notes' when you want to say something is perfect. 'Notes' in this context refers to feedback or criticism, just like when a teacher assesses a piece of work and leaves notes for future improvement.

Georgie
Right. So, if you say 'no notes', you are expressing that you have no feedback or criticism. Whatever you're talking about is perfect or flawless.

Feifei
So, you used it in the context of a singer's performance. I used it when talking about my perfect week. Now, time for some more examples.

Examples
That three-course meal was incredibly delicious. No notes.

I went to a wedding, and the best man's speech was hilarious. No notes.

Wow. Your outfit is stunning. No notes.

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习表达 “no notes” 的用法。单词 “note”指的是 “批注” 或 “评语”。所以，“no notes” 听起来像是在说 “批改作业或试卷时没有留下任何修改意见”，而我们实际上用它来表示 “我觉得这件事无可挑剔、十分完美，一点意见也没有。”

Georgie, is the expression 'no notes' always used on its own, without a verb?

Georgie
Yes. Most commonly, it is used on its own, but you might also hear a sentence like 'I have no notes'.

Feifei
在使用 “no notes” 的时侯，我们既可以单独使用它，强调某事 “很完美，没什么可挑剔的”，也可以把它放在句中使用，比如，“I have no notes”，意思就是 “我没意见，我完全同意”。

Georgie
OK, let's recap. 'No notes' is a modern slang expression that is used when something is perfect, and no negative feedback is needed.

Feifei
Thank you for joining us. Goodbye!

Georgie
Bye-bye!

item.title: Say less 懂了，不必多说
item.description:
节目简介

就像 “say no more” 的意思并非字面上的 “别说了”，而是在告诉别人 “你不用再说了，我都懂” 一样，新兴表达 “say less” 的意思也不是 “少说点”，而是 “我懂了，你不用再多说了，我完全同意”。听节目，跟主持人菲菲和 Georgie 一起来学习这个年轻一代常用的新潮表达。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Feifei
Hello and welcome to Authentic Real English, where we explain expressions used by fluent English speakers so that you can use them, too! I'm Feifei, and I'm joined by Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
I'm very well, thank you Feifei. How are you?

Feifei
I'm very well too, thank you. Now, it's time to introduce a new expression to our listeners. I think let's teach a modern phrase this time, Georgie. Have you got any of those?

Georgie
Say less, Feifei.

Feifei
What? Are you telling me to stop speaking?

Georgie
No! I mean I understand. I'm with you! Let's teach a modern expression.

Feifei
Is 'say less' a modern expression?

Georgie
It is. 'Say less' was popularised on social media and is used in informal, everyday speech. You can use 'say less' when you understand someone fully and don't need further explanation, or when they've suggested a great plan and you don't need further convincing.

Feifei
OK, but it sounds quite friendly, so I guess it's used to show enthusiastic agreement, rather than hinting that someone should stop speaking.

Georgie
Exactly. Shall we hear some more examples?

Feifei
Say less, Georgie.

Examples
My boss asked me if I was ready to go on a break after a 15-hour shift. I said, "Say less! Get me out of here."

My friend said the dress code for their party was 'all black', and I said, "Say less! I don't have anything colourful in my wardrobe."

You're asking me if I want an ice cream on this boiling hot day? Say less!

Feifei
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “地道英语” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习流行表达 “say less” 的用法。“Say less” 的字面意思是 “少说点”。但它的实际含义和表达 “say no more” 非常接近，就是 “我明白你的意思了，不用再多说了” 或者 “我完全同意”。相比之下，“say less” 不仅更加简短，也更具现代感和潮流感。

Georgie
That's right. And there are some other, similar expressions too. If a good plan has been suggested, of course you could say 'say less', but you could also say 'I'm in' or 'I'm sold' if you've been persuaded. Shall we grab coffee after this, Feifei?

Feifei
I'm sold on that idea, Georgie.

在口语中，如果别人提出了一个我们赞同或支持的意见、想法或计划，除了用 “say less” 表示赞同之外，我们还可以用 “I'm in” 和 “I'm sold” 来回应。“I'm in” 的意思是 “算我一个” 或者 “我加入”；“I'm sold” 的意思是 “你把我说服了，这个想法我买账”。

Georgie
OK. Time to recap. Use 'say less' when you want to enthusiastically agree with someone after they have suggested something.

Feifei
Thank you for joining us. Goodbye!

Georgie
Bye-bye!
